United States.plan: ACA marketplace plan before 65, Medicare from 65
United States.notes: Priced by the ACA / Medicare model in the kernel. Original Medicare has no out-of-pocket cap unless a Medigap or Medicare Advantage plan is added.

Panama.notes: Midpoint of broker ranges at a moderate deductible: about $250-500 per adult per month at 60, $500-1,200 at 70. Not quotes. The social security system (CSS) is for workers and voluntary entry reportedly closes at 57 (women) / 62 (men); public MINSA facilities are a pay-per-use backstop. Most insurers stop accepting new members between 55 and 75, and pre-existing conditions are usually excluded or surcharged.

Costa Rica.notes: Mandatory for legal residents; pre-existing conditions covered, no age limit. Contribution is roughly 7-11% of declared income with a $1,000/month floor for pensionados, so the stored line understates the cost for higher declared pensions.

Spain.notes: Available after 12 months of registered residence: about EUR 60/month per person under 65 and EUR 157 from 65; pre-existing conditions covered; outpatient prescriptions not included. A private policy without co-pays is required for the non-lucrative visa before that.

Portugal.notes: Open to registered legal residents at low co-pays; family-doctor assignment can take months. Private insurance is required for the D7 visa, and Portuguese private plans often cap entry at 65-70.

France.notes: Residence-based after a 3-month wait for people with no professional activity. A new financial participation for certain non-working residents (Article L160-1-1) has no published amount yet, so the stored line may understate the cost for visitor-visa retirees.

Italy.notes: Annual fee of EUR 2,000 minimum (4% of income above EUR 31,923.99, capped at EUR 2,788.87), by calendar year and not pro-rated; a dependent spouse is covered by the same payment; pre-existing conditions covered. A private policy or SSN enrolment satisfies the elective-residence visa.

Greece.plan: EOPYY optional insurance for third-country pensioners
Greece.notes: Optional for holders of a pensioner residence permit at 8.5% of pension income, so the stored line understates the cost for higher pensions. Whether passive-income permits qualify is not confirmed.

Cyprus.plan: Private health insurance (GESY not open to non-EU retiree permit holders)
Cyprus.notes: Non-EU nationals qualify for GESY only if employed, permanently resident or family of a beneficiary. No sourced age-banded private premium yet; the stored healthcare line is not a catastrophic premium.

Malta.notes: No source could be read on 2026-11-16. Classified from general knowledge that third-country retirement permits require private cover. No sourced premium; the stored healthcare line is not a catastrophic premium.

Ireland.plan: Private medical insurance at or above VHI Plan D level
Ireland.notes: Stamp 0 holders cannot use public hospitals; private cover with at least EUR 25,000 in-hospital cover is mandatory at every renewal. No sourced age-banded premium yet.

Croatia.notes: Mandatory for residents after 90 days; quoted at about $85-225 per person per month with 20% co-pays, and non-EU applicants may owe the previous 12 months of premiums on first registration.

Mexico.notes: Open to temporary and permanent residents; about 18,300 pesos per year for a person in their 60s. Applicants with listed pre-existing conditions (including malignant tumours and chronic degenerative disease) cannot enrol, in which case a private major-medical plan is needed and is not priced here.

Colombia.plan: Prepaid medicine (medicina prepagada) or international plan
Colombia.notes: Sources conflict on whether retirement-visa holders can join the public EPS (one says excluded since October 2022). Prepaid plans are quoted at about $75-180 per person per month without age bands; visa applicants must carry insurance with repatriation cover.

Ecuador.notes: About $83/month, or $97 with a spouse, scaling with declared income; reported to cover pre-existing conditions without exclusions; long waits.

Uruguay.notes: Mutualistas run about $100-200 per person per month; many cap new members at 60-65, some accept older members for a buy-in fee. ASSE has no age or pre-existing restriction.
